description.value: A family-owned general store in the rural community of Rosswood, operating since 1983 and housed in a historic building originally used as an Officer's Mess during World War II. Located along the Nisga'a Highway corridor near Terrace, it stocks everyday essentials, fresh farm eggs, bulk foods, locally made goods, and specialty products—a rare resupply point in a remote stretch of Northern BC. The current owner took over in 2012 and has continued the store's role as a central community gathering place.

address.value: 4185 Kalum Lake Drive, Terrace, BC V8G 0G8

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A well-established general store on a remote Northern BC highway corridor stocking everyday essentials and bulk foods—a valuable resupply stop for touring cyclists with few alternatives in the area.
enrichment_extras.notes: The store explicitly acknowledges it is located on unceded Kitsumkalum First Nation traditional territory. A journal post titled '5 Things to do in Rosswood' promotes a scenic drive up the Nisga'a Highway along Kitsumkalum Lake, suggesting the area has tourism appeal for cyclists on that route.
